{{Short description|Mathematical constant}}
{{Use shortened footnotes|date=May 2021}}
'''Bernstein's constant''', usually denoted by the Greek letter β ([[Beta (letter)|beta]]), is a [[mathematical constant]] named after [[Sergei Natanovich Bernstein]] and is equal to 0.2801694990... .{{r|OEIS_A073001}}

== Definition ==
Let ''E''<sub>''n''</sub>(ƒ) be the error of the best [[uniform approximation]] to a [[real function]] ''ƒ''(''x'') on the interval [&minus;1,&nbsp;1] by real polynomials of no more than degree ''n''. In the case of ''ƒ''(''x'')&nbsp;=&nbsp;|''x''|, Bernstein{{r|Bernstein1914}} showed that the limit 

:<math>\beta=\lim_{n \to \infty}2nE_{2n}(f),\,</math>

called '''Bernstein's constant''', exists and is between 0.278 and 0.286. His [[conjecture]] that the limit is:

:<math>\frac {1}{2\sqrt {\pi}}=0.28209\dots\,.</math>

was disproven by Varga and Carpenter,{{r|VargaCarpenter1987}} who calculated 

:<math>\beta=0.280169499023\dots\,.</math>
